title: fix(app-shell): a rolled-back Studio publish shows its "Nothing was published" banner again (objectui#11985)
body:
Fixes #11985
Clause-②: no

## What changes

Studio's publish message comes from `formatPublishFailures` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/metadataError.ts`. It told a rolled-back sibling apart with `BATCH_ABORTED_CODE = 'batch_aborted'`, compared with `===`. But `publishPackageDrafts` gives each rolled-back sibling `code: 'BATCH_ABORTED'`. So the banner branch never ran, and the author got one parallel line per draft.

- `BATCH_ABORTED_CODE` is now `'BATCH_ABORTED'` and is compared exactly, with no case-folding (triage direction `6063923729`).
- The literal is tied to the spec's error-code ledger with `'BATCH_ABORTED' satisfies RegisteredErrorCode`, through `import type { RegisteredErrorCode } from '@objectstack/spec/api'`.
  - The spec exports no runtime constant for this one code. Its only exported source is the ledger (`ERROR_CODE_LEDGER`), and importing that at runtime would add bytes.
  - The type-only import is erased at build time. The emitted literal has the same 13 characters as before, so first-load bytes should not move. The PR's `Bundle Analysis` is the reading.
  - `RegisteredErrorCode` and the ledger's `'BATCH_ABORTED'` entry are in both `@objectstack/spec@17.6.0` (the floor of app-shell's range) and `17.7.0` (the lockfile's resolution).
- The docblock on `PublishFailure.code` and the docblock on the function now name the producer's spelling.
- `packages/app-shell/src/preview/publishRefusal.ts`, comment only: its header gave this renderer's case bug as one reason the package doors do not reuse `formatPublishFailures`. That sentence is now false. It is replaced by the reason that still holds (the English banner) and a note on how the two compare the code.
- The callers are unchanged. Both toast branches of `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`'s `doPublish`, and the AI chat page's publish summary, get the fix through the formatter.
- Changeset: `.changeset/11985-batch-aborted-banner.md`, `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`. Nothing is added to the package entry: `BATCH_ABORTED_CODE` and `formatPublishFailures` are not exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`.

## Tests

- In `metadataError.test.ts`, the existing fixtures now use the producer's spelling (`BATCH_ABORTED`, `INVALID_METADATA`).
- New describe block `formatPublishFailures on the producer rollback answer (objectui#11985)`:
  - **The pin.** A causal `object/lead` plus two `BATCH_ABORTED` siblings, each carrying the producer's own sentence. The output has three lines: the "Nothing was published" banner first, then `object/lead: failed spec validation`, then `2 other drafts aborted`. Neither sibling is listed.
  - **The control.** The causal item alone keeps its own line and shows no banner.
- **Reverse verification 1 (behaviour):** `ablation-replace` put back the old `export const BATCH_ABORTED_CODE = 'batch_aborted';` with anchor 1 to 0 and blob `bf192cc32060` to `19ad0503540a`. Result: `Tests  3 failed | 2 passed (5)`.
  - Red: the new pin and the two existing banner cases.
  - Green: the control and the parallel-lines case.
  - Restored with blob == HEAD (`bf192cc32060`) and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Reverse verification 2 (the type tie):** the literal was changed to `'BATCH_ABORTEDX'` and `tsc --noEmit` failed with `error TS1360: Type '"BATCH_ABORTEDX"' does not satisfy the expected type` (the ledger union). So the check reads the built spec type, not a cache. It was restored with blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. The old lower-case spelling would fail the same way, so a return to it no longer compiles.

## Gates (all at HEAD `34eda28f5`, run from the worktree root)

- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`, `TURBO_EXIT=0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.ts`): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on `metadataError.test.ts` alone: `Tests  5 passed (5)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on the narrowed publish-path set, 15 files: `Test Files  15 passed (15)`, `Tests  76 passed (76)`.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three touched `.ts` files, `--format json`: 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:test-path-roots`, `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`: each exit 0, each with its own OK line.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four paths: `NOT GOVERNED`.

**Declared narrowing: the whole `packages/app-shell/` suite was NOT MEASURED locally.** CI runs all of it in its shards.
- The full run (1192 test files, `--maxWorkers=2`) held the shared verify lock for 29m51s without finishing, while another dev's run waited behind it. I stopped my own run (exit 143).
- The narrowed set is every test file in the repo that spells either form of the code (`git grep -il batch_aborted` over `*.test.ts` and `*.test.tsx`: three files, `metadataError.test.ts` among them as the positive control). It also includes every publish-path test of both callers and of the two sibling doors.
- Why that set is enough: the only runtime change is the value of a constant read only inside `formatPublishFailures`, and no test imports it. So a test's verdict can change only if it sends a code spelled `batch_aborted` or `BATCH_ABORTED` through that function.
- Lint narrowing:
  - The population comes from `eslint.config.js`: its `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` blocks cover the three touched `.ts` files, and the changeset `.md` is outside every `files` glob.
  - The JSON output counts 3 files.
  - Invariance: the config sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware. No rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch.

## Acceptance notes

- **The two kinds of comparison now differ, for the seat to route.**
  - This formatter matches `BATCH_ABORTED` exactly, as triage directed.
  - The sibling doors from objectui#11922 (`refusedItemsText` in `publishRefusal.ts`, and the rollback check in `PackagesPage.tsx`'s `publishDrafts`) still use `errorCodeIs(f, 'BATCH_ABORTED')`, which ignores case.
  - Those two comparisons are off this claim's surface and were not touched.
- `AiChatPage.tsx` (a caller, off the surface) keeps a code comment that describes the publish answer as an item plus `batch_aborted` markers. That comment now names a spelling the producer never emits. It is prose only. Carrier: the next PR that touches that file. Noted here, not filed.
- Premise, re-read before the first edit:
  - objectstack `origin/main` `7b926f76`, `publishPackageDrafts` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`: the rollback branch sets `code: 'BATCH_ABORTED'` on each sibling.
  - The spec at the `@objectstack/spec@17.6.0` and `17.7.0` tags lists `'BATCH_ABORTED'` in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER`.
  - objectui `fff07fbba` had the lower-case constant and lower-case fixtures.
- Claim: `6064407722`. A second claim (`6064415932`) arrived 28 s later and was withdrawn in `6064445227` before the first edit.
